metadata.title: Ideal Bernoulli Flow Between Two Pipe Sections
metadata.topic: Continuity and Bernoulli behaviour in a horizontal contraction

learningPurpose: Support a visual comparison of cross-sectional area, average velocity, absolute pressure, and ideal head at two points in a horizontal circular pipe.

definitions.meaning: Fluid volume passing a section per unit time.
For the steady incompressible two-section model, the same volumetric flow rate passes both sections, so area and average velocity vary inversely.
An ideal mechanical-energy relationship linking pressure, average velocity, and elevation along the modelled flow path under stated assumptions.

governingPrinciples: For steady incompressible flow without leakage, A1 v1 = A2 v2. [SRC-OPENSTAX-COLLEGE-PHYSICS-2E-2022]
For the ideal frictionless model, the sum of pressure, kinetic, and elevation terms is conserved between two points. [SRC-OPENSTAX-COLLEGE-PHYSICS-2E-2022]
The Bernoulli relationship is restricted by steady, incompressible, inviscid assumptions and excludes added heat or shaft work in this pilot. [SRC-NASA-GLENN-BERNOULLI]

equations.name: Average velocity from flow rate and area
Two-point Bernoulli equation
equations.expression: P1 + rho*v1^2/2 + rho*g*z1 = P2 + rho*v2^2/2 + rho*g*z2

symbolDefinitions.name: section 1 elevation above the selected reference
section 2 elevation above the selected reference

assumptions: Steady, incompressible, frictionless flow along the stated path.
Horizontal pipe: z1 = z2 = 0 m relative to the selected datum.
No leakage, pump work, turbine work, heat transfer, or loss term.
Density is the fixed model parameter 1000 kg/m^3; it is not presented as a universal fluid property.
Inlet absolute pressure is the fixed educational model parameter 250000 Pa.
Animated flow indicators communicate direction and relative state only; they are not particle trajectories or a time solution.
limitations: No viscosity, pipe roughness, fittings, turbulence, compressibility, cavitation, transient flow, or equipment rating model is included.
The result does not establish professional pipe, pump, nozzle, or process design sufficiency.
Interaction ranges are educational model bounds rather than manufacturer limits.
Independent engineering and educational review remains required before student-use approval.

workedExample.title: Horizontal contraction at the default state
workedExample.purpose: Connect flow rate, diameter, average velocity, and ideal pressure change.
steps: Calculate A1 and A2 from each circular diameter.
Calculate v1 = Q/A1 and v2 = Q/A2.
Apply the two-point Bernoulli equation to calculate P2.
Compare pressure and velocity head at both points.
workedExample.answer: The smaller second section has the greater average velocity and lower ideal absolute pressure; the total ideal head is conserved within rounding.

normalOperation: The same modelled volumetric flow rate passes both sections.
Reducing section 2 diameter reduces area and increases section 2 average velocity.
At equal elevation in the ideal model, an increase in velocity corresponds to a decrease in static pressure.

safety.hazard: Applying an ideal educational relationship as a real equipment design or operating limit
safety.warning: The lab omits losses, transients, cavitation, structural limits, and equipment ratings.
safety.studentBoundary: Use the result only to explain the ideal relationship inside the declared model range.
